defects_found.description: File absent from W\freeze\ at check time (confirmed via directory listing). Per task instruction this is noted for the orchestrator rather than treated as a failure, since it may still be in progress by a parallel agent. Its stated scope (exactly the two medium_low rows, 005 and 017) matches freeze_summary.json's confidence_spread (medium_low: 2) and the two medium_low rows actually present in frozen_rows_final.jsonl (M8-Ruth-005, M8-Ruth-017), so the target set is verifiable even though the sidecar content itself could not be inspected.

Challenge OL-M8-Ruth-005-1 is filed once (home decision M8-Ruth-005) and receives exactly one boss ruling (under M8-Ruth-005 in boss_rulings.json), but its author-response ripple is recorded under three decisions (M8-Ruth-001, M8-Ruth-005, M8-Ruth-015) because the underlying defect - an unstated qualifier for a disjunctive-clause construction shared by all three verses - required a single principle to be stated identically in all three rationales. This is documented and intentional: boss_rulings.json._meta.decision_relations note M8-Ruth-REL-002 explicitly links 005 and 015 on this basis, and the M8-Ruth-001/005/015 rationales now state the identical two-part test verbatim. Flagged only so the orchestrator is aware a strict 1-challenge-to-1-response count undercounts this row; it is not a process violation and required no correction.

Confirmed non-empty (19 decisions, pre-revision plain-accent baseline) and consistent with frozen_rows_final.jsonl as the pre-image the challenge/response cycle improved on (e.g. M8-Ruth-001's draft lacks the 005/015 cross-reference and carries the uncorrected לָתֶת typo later fixed). Included only as a corroborating provenance note, not a defect.
